pages.title: About
pages.content:
About Eiyo Clinic

Since 2016

Seattle, 418 Alder Row

We started in 2016 with one table,

two chairs and a pencil.

Most of what we do is still

sitting down and writing it out together.

Eiyo Clinic was founded in 2016 to offer calm, practical nutrition support grounded in ordinary everyday food. We work from a quiet building on Alder Row in Seattle, helping adults build sustainable eating routines.

We started with one table

We started in 2016 with one table, two chairs, and a simple premise: most of eating well comes down to plain, repeatable meals. Many people arrive at our clinic exhausted by contradictory rules, restrictive programmes, and elaborate recipes that collapse under the pressure of a busy week. Our goal is never to overhaul your kitchen overnight or demand perfection. Instead, we sit down with you to look at your actual schedule, your cooking habits, and the foods you already enjoy. From that foundation, we build manageable meals that fit into an ordinary Tuesday: a breakfast you will genuinely prepare before leaving home, a lunch that travels well, and simple evening cooking that does not leave you drained.

Why plain meals work

In our experience, health is sustained by meals that are straightforward and predictable rather than complex or restrictive. When advice requires weighing ingredients, tracking numbers, or preparing separate dishes from the rest of your household, it rarely survives stressful periods. Plain meals rely on staple groceries: wholegrains, eggs, beans, seasonal vegetables, fruit, and straightforward proteins that can be assembled quickly without special equipment. By focusing on steady nourishment rather than novelty, you reduce the mental burden of deciding what to eat three times a day. This steady approach gives your body consistent energy and creates a calm routine you can keep up across months and years.

How we work alongside your doctor

Dietitians at Eiyo Clinic work alongside your doctor, not in place of them. If you have been diagnosed with high cholesterol, elevated blood sugar, or other chronic health considerations, your physician oversees your clinical treatment and medication. Our role is to translate their medical recommendations into practical groceries, kitchen routines, and plate choices that make sense in daily life. With your permission, we send summary notes directly to your primary care clinic following your consultations, ensuring your healthcare team remains coordinated. We never alter prescribed therapies or promise medical cures; we focus entirely on the everyday eating patterns that support your ongoing care.

The building on Alder Row

Our clinic occupies one quiet floor at 418 Alder Row, Suite 2, in Seattle. We designed the space to feel calm and welcoming, deliberately avoiding the cold aesthetic of an institutional examination suite. The clinic houses three private consult rooms, each arranged around a plain wooden table and soft natural light from large curtained windows, alongside one dedicated teaching kitchen for hands-on classes. Having both consult spaces and a working kitchen in the same location allows us to move seamlessly from planning meals on paper to practicing knife skills and simple preparation techniques. The building is step-free, accessible, and easily reached by public transit.

pages.title: Approach
pages.content:
A plan written with you, not for you.

60 min

First consults have mornings open

Book, talk, plan,

and then come back.

Nothing here is a rule to memorise,

only a plan you wrote with us.

Nutrition support at Eiyo Clinic is collaborative, realistic, and tailored to your actual life. We look at where everyday routines stall and help you create manageable habits that last.

Most eating difficulties do not stem from a lack of willpower; they happen when daily routines collide with unreasonable expectations. Through years of clinical practice, we have found that eating typically breaks down at three familiar friction points: skipped breakfast in the rush to leave the house, late dinners eaten hastily after long workdays, and all-or-nothing weeks where rigid meal prep gives way to complete exhaustion by Wednesday night. When you understand why these stalls happen in your specific environment, you can stop blaming yourself and begin designing realistic solutions that protect your energy throughout the day.

How one consult runs

Four stages, written by hand: book, talk, plan, follow up.

Before you come

Book a first consult. We send a three-day food note. Write what you ate, not what you should have.

Booking

In the room, 60 minutes

We read your note together, pick two changes, and write the plan by hand.

After the visit

Your typed plan reaches you within 2 working days. Follow-ups at weeks 2, 6 and 12.

Fees

Plainer meals, planned together.

Before you come: the three-day food note

Your work with us begins before you step into our rooms. Once you book a first consult, we send you a simple three-day food note. We ask you to record whatever you actually eat and drink over three ordinary days, including snacks, coffee, and late-night bites. There is no need to weigh food or tally calories, and you should never change your eating habits to impress us. Write what you ate, not what you think you should have eaten. This note provides an honest, non-judgmental snapshot of your current rhythm, showing us your appetite patterns, energy dips, and daily constraints.

In the room: the 60-minute consult

During your 60-minute first consult, we sit down together at a light oak table to review your three-day note. Rather than handing you a generic pre-printed sheet, we talk through your typical mornings, work demands, and family commitments. Together, we identify two practical adjustments to start with—perhaps adding protein to your morning coffee or stocking a reliable afternoon snack at your desk. We draft your plan by hand with a pencil right there across the table, ensuring every recommendation feels realistic to you. A clean, typed copy is delivered to your inbox within 2 working days.

After the visit: structured follow-ups

Lasting dietary change requires ongoing reflection rather than one-time instruction. Our care follows a structured four-stage flow: initial booking and your three-day food note, the 60-minute first consult, your typed plan delivered within 2 working days, and targeted follow-up sessions scheduled at weeks 2, 6, and 12. These follow-ups give you time to test your new routines in real life. We review what worked smoothly, adjust strategies that felt cumbersome, and troubleshoot new challenges like travel, social dinners, or shifting work schedules, helping your habits remain stable over time.

Everyday eating consultations

Everyday eating consultations are designed for adults seeking steady energy and simpler kitchen routines without rigid dieting. We examine your daily schedule, meal timing, and relationship with food, replacing confusion with dependable, balanced meals. Whether you struggle with afternoon slumps, disorganized grocery shopping, or mealtime indecision, we help you build a clear personal framework. Consultations are available as a single 60-minute initial visit or through our structured three-month care plan, providing the continuous guidance and accountability needed to make balanced eating second nature.

Blood sugar and cholesterol support

When routine lab work indicates elevated fasting blood glucose, rising HbA1c, or shifting cholesterol markers, food choices can feel daunting and fraught with anxiety. Our registered dietitians work directly alongside your doctor to translate clinical targets into reassuring, satisfying meals. We focus on soluble fiber, quality fats, and regular meal spacing that protect cardiovascular health and stabilize energy. We do not promote extreme carbohydrate restriction or unproven supplements. Instead, we establish sustainable dietary patterns that support your medical treatment and fit comfortably into your normal family meals.

Family meals and shift work

We offer dedicated support for complex household schedules. Our family meals consult is a 75-minute session for up to four household members, helping you create adaptable dinners where everyone eats the same core meal with minor personal adjustments. For healthcare workers, transit staff, and frequent travelers, our shift work consultations address the physical disruption of rotating rosters and frequent dining out. We design timing strategies that maintain digestive comfort and mental alertness through long overnights, ensuring you stay nourished without relying entirely on takeout or vending machines.

Grocery walk

To turn ideas into practical skills, we offer hands-on educational sessions outside the consult room. Our 45-minute grocery walk takes place at a neighborhood food store near our Alder Row clinic, navigating the aisles together to demystify ingredient labels, compare pantry staples, and identify quick meal components.

45 minutes, $80.

Kitchen class

Back at the clinic, our two-hour kitchen classes welcome small groups of up to six participants into our teaching kitchen. Led by our cook, Priya Raman, these relaxed sessions emphasize foundational knife work, batch cooking basics, and simple vegetable preparation.

2 hours, up to 6 people, $45 each.

pages.title: Dietitians
pages.content:
Seven people, three rooms.

7 people

3 rooms and a teaching kitchen

Seven people, three rooms,

one teaching kitchen.

Everyone here eats lunch,

and most of us cook it.

Eiyo Clinic brings together experienced registered dietitians, an educator cook, and dedicated front desk support. We share a calm, collaborative approach centered on unpretentious everyday nutrition.

Ingrid Solberg

Founder & Registered Dietitian

Ingrid founded Eiyo Clinic in 2016 after years in community health, believing clinical nutrition should center on plain, accessible food rather than restrictive trends. She specializes in general adult nutrition, foundational habit formation, and collaborative meal planning. Across sixty-minute consults, Ingrid helps clients strip away guilt and establish predictable, nourishing routines. She oversees clinic methodology and mentors our clinical team on Alder Row.

Tomás Ávila

Registered Dietitian

Tomás focuses on metabolic health, particularly guiding adults managing elevated blood sugar, pre-diabetes, and high cholesterol. He works closely alongside your physician to align nutrition strategies with medical guidance, emphasizing soluble fibers, wholesome grains, and realistic portion patterns. Tomás is known for his calm, analytical approach, helping clients interpret their lab results without panic and turn medical recommendations into enjoyable, sustainable dinners.

Amara Nwosu

Registered Dietitian

Amara leads our family nutrition consultations, helping busy households navigate varied taste preferences, conflicting schedules, and dinner table tension. She specializes in adaptable meal planning where one balanced foundation serves multiple family members with minimal fuss. Amara holds advanced training in adult nutrition and pediatric feeding dynamics, bringing warmth, humor, and immense practical patience to our consulting rooms on Alder Row.

Leila Haddad

Registered Dietitian

Leila supports clients working irregular hours, including healthcare professionals, emergency staff, rotating shift workers, and frequent business travelers. She understands the physiological strain that circadian disruption places on digestion, appetite, and energy. Leila works collaboratively to build resilient meal routines, packable meals that endure twelve-hour shifts, and mindful restaurant strategies that keep energy stable without requiring unattainable kitchen perfection.

Daniel Brennan

Registered Dietitian

Daniel assists adults seeking to incorporate more plant-forward eating into their lives, whether transitioning toward vegetarian eating or simply adding more legumes, nuts, and seasonal vegetables. He emphasizes culinary practicality, nutrient adequacy, and uncomplicated preparation over rigid dietary labels. Daniel ensures clients meet iron, protein, and micronutrient requirements comfortably while enjoying flavorful, grounding food that suits their lifestyle and values.

Priya Raman

Kitchen Educator & Cook

Priya directs our small-group cooking classes inside the clinic's teaching kitchen. A dedicated cook with deep expertise in home kitchen efficiency, she teaches knife safety, basic roasting methods, grain cookery, and modular batch preparation. Priya believes that cooking confidence begins with basic mechanical skills, creating a welcoming, tactile environment where up to six adults can practice preparing simple meals together.

Sofia Marchetti

Front Desk & Client Care

Sofia coordinates appointment scheduling, client intake, and general reception at our Seattle office. She manages our three-day food note distribution, answers questions regarding appointment logistics, and assists clients with itemized superbills for insurance reimbursement. Sofia ensures the clinic remains a quiet, orderly, and reassuring environment from the moment you call or step through our door at 418 Alder Row.

pages.title: Stories
pages.content:
Three people, three ordinary weeks.

3 stories

Shared with consent

Real nutritional change happens quietly over ordinary weeks and domestic routines. These three experiences illustrate how individual planning helped clients find sustainable rhythms.

Dietitian: Tomás Ávila

Mark, 54 — breakfast back on the table

Mark, 54, came to Eiyo Clinic after a routine physical showed shifting cholesterol numbers and his doctor advised reviewing his daily eating. For nearly a decade, Mark had skipped breakfast entirely, surviving on black coffee until an overwhelming afternoon hunger triggered unplanned snacking and heavy takeout dinners. Working alongside dietitian Tomás Ávila, Mark began by completing a three-day food note. Rather than demanding an elaborate morning menu, Tomás helped Mark identify two manageable breakfasts he could reliably assemble in under five minutes: rolled oats with fruit and walnuts, or toasted wholegrain bread with hard-boiled eggs. Over follow-up appointments at weeks 2, 6, and 12, Mark rebuilt a consistent morning appetite. His afternoon energy slumps subsided, and dinner naturally became lighter and more balanced. Shared with consent, with personal details changed.

Shared with consent; details changed.

Dietitian: Leila Haddad

Rosa, 38, night-shift nurse — a lunch that lasts a 12-hour shift

Rosa, 38, works as a night-shift nurse in an acute hospital unit, navigating exhausting twelve-hour shifts that frequently left her reliant on vending machine snacks and cold cafeteria leftovers. Disturbed sleep and erratic meal timing had left her digestive system uncomfortable and her stamina depleted. She booked a consult with dietitian Leila Haddad to develop a realistic strategy for shift work. Together, they designed meals that could withstand hours in a shared breakroom refrigerator and be eaten quickly in fifteen-minute intervals. Rosa began packing sturdy grain salads with chickpeas, sliced vegetables, and pumpkin seeds, alongside portable snacks like yogurt and whole fruit. Within six weeks, Rosa reported steady alertness through the 3:00 a.m. hospital lull and far less nausea when returning home to sleep. Shared with consent, with personal details changed.

Shared with consent; details changed.

Dietitian: Amara Nwosu

The Okafor-Lindh household — one dinner, four plates

The Okafor-Lindh family struggled with the nightly friction of feeding four household members with conflicting extracurricular schedules, distinct appetite sizes, and differing food preferences. Dinner had devolved into cooking three separate meals or ordering last-minute delivery. The family scheduled a 75-minute family meals consultation with dietitian Amara Nwosu to establish common ground. Amara introduced a modular dinner framework centered on a single versatile base—such as roasted root vegetables, brown rice, or warm lentil stew—paired with simple customizable toppings like toasted seeds, cheese, or sliced chicken. This allowed both the parents and teenagers to assemble a plate matching their individual preferences without creating extra pots or kitchen chaos. After three months, weeknight dinners felt collaborative and calm rather than frantic. Shared with consent, with personal details changed.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.content:
Questions, answered plainly.

Phone or online

Book a first consult

Here are straightforward answers to common questions about our nutrition consultations, billing practices, and clinical approach. If you need further assistance, please contact our desk.

Do I need a doctor's referral to schedule a consultation?

You do not need a formal physician referral to book a consultation at Eiyo Clinic. Many adults contact us directly to improve their everyday eating habits, establish reliable breakfast routines, or navigate busy work schedules. However, if you are seeking guidance for diagnosed medical conditions such as high cholesterol, hypertension, or elevated blood glucose, we strongly encourage sharing your doctor's details. With your permission, our dietitians will coordinate with your primary care provider and send them summary notes after your visits, ensuring your nutritional changes safely complement your ongoing medical care.

Can dietitians at Eiyo Clinic prescribe medication or supplements?

Our practitioners are registered dietitians, not medical doctors, and we do not prescribe pharmaceuticals or recommend unproven supplement regimens. If your health condition requires medical intervention or prescription medication, your physician manages those treatments. Our focus remains squarely on food, meal composition, grocery choices, and daily kitchen habits. When appropriate, we may suggest standard dietary adjustments to help you meet recommended daily micronutrient levels through regular groceries like legumes, nuts, seeds, and leafy greens, always in full coordination with your medical doctor.

Do you offer video consultations for remote clients?

Yes, we provide 30-minute video follow-up appointments for established clients at a rate of $60 per session. While we strongly encourage attending your 60-minute initial consult in person at our Seattle clinic on Alder Row, subsequent check-ins can take place over our secure telehealth video platform. Remote visits are ideal for reviewing your ongoing progress, discussing dining out challenges, or adjusting your plan when work or family commitments make traveling to the clinic difficult. You need only a computer or tablet with a reliable internet connection.

Do you work with children or entire families?

While our core practice focuses on adult nutrition, we offer a dedicated 75-minute family meals consultation for $150 that accommodates up to four household members, including teenagers. We do not provide clinical pediatric diets or restrictive eating plans for young children. Instead, our family sessions focus on household harmony, meal timing, and establishing a single, adaptable evening meal that parents and children can share comfortably. Our goal is to reduce dinner table conflict, simplify cooking duties, and make shared family dinners manageable and enjoyable for everyone.

How does insurance reimbursement work for your services?

Eiyo Clinic operates as a self-pay clinic and does not bill insurance companies directly. Payment is completed by credit or debit card at the time of your appointment. However, we routinely provide clients with a detailed, itemized superbill upon request. This receipt includes clinical procedure codes, provider identifiers, and diagnosis details that you can submit directly to your private insurer for potential out-of-network reimbursement. Because coverage for medical nutrition therapy varies widely across policies, we suggest calling your insurer beforehand to verify your specific out-of-network benefits.

What should I prepare before attending my first consult?

Before arriving for your initial 60-minute consult, we ask that you complete the three-day food note that our front desk emails to you upon booking. Please record everything you eat and drink across three ordinary days, including snacks and beverages. Be entirely candid; do not alter your eating habits to look healthier, and do not worry about measuring exact portions or calculating calories. In addition, please bring a list of any routine medications you take, along with recent bloodwork or lab summaries from your doctor if you have them.

What is your appointment cancellation and rescheduling policy?

We understand that illness, urgent work deadlines, and personal emergencies can arise unexpectedly. You may reschedule or cancel any scheduled appointment free of charge provided you notify us at least 24 hours prior to your session time. If an appointment is cancelled with less than 24 hours of advance notice or missed without contact, the full session fee is charged to the card on file. This policy respects our dietitians' dedicated preparation time and allows us to offer open slots to clients waiting for care.

How are follow-up visits scheduled after the first appointment?

Following your 60-minute initial consultation and the delivery of your typed nutrition plan, we typically schedule follow-up appointments at weeks 2, 6, and 12. The two-week check-in allows us to troubleshoot immediate obstacles with your new routines, while the six-week and twelve-week visits help solidify long-term consistency. Follow-ups can be booked individually as 30-minute in-person visits ($65) or video visits ($60), or purchased together as part of our comprehensive three-month care plan ($295). We adjust the spacing to fit your life.

posts.title: The Case for the Plain Breakfast
posts.excerpt: Building a calm, repeatable morning meal is the most dependable way to stabilize energy and eliminate frantic eating decisions throughout the day.
posts.content:
When people decide to pay closer attention to their nutrition, their instinct is often to start with dinner. They imagine complex grain bowls, elaborate vegetable prep, and restrictive kitchen rules that demand hours of evening cooking. Yet in our clinical consult rooms on Alder Row, we almost always look in the opposite direction. We start with breakfast. Not because breakfast holds magical metabolic powers, but because morning is the point in the day where routines are most fragile and small improvements yield the most immediate calm.

Most of the adults who visit our Seattle clinic describe a morning rhythm that is rushed, disjointed, and unpredictable. Many skip breakfast entirely, relying on black coffee to carry them through morning meetings until an abrupt mid-afternoon energy crash forces an emergency visit to the nearest pastry counter or vending machine. Others attempt intricate morning smoothies or high-protein recipes they found online, only to abandon them by Wednesday when cleaning a blender before eight in the morning proves unmanageable. The result is a cycle of morning restriction followed by evening exhaustion.

A plain breakfast breaks that cycle by removing the burden of decision-making. Eating well does not require culinary innovation at dawn; it requires predictability. When you establish a morning meal that requires five minutes or less to assemble, uses humble pantry staples, and tastes genuinely satisfying, you protect your future self from the volatile hunger swings that derail later choices. You do not have to wonder what to eat, weigh ingredients on a kitchen scale, or feel guilty about keeping things simple.

In practice, a dependable breakfast is built from ordinary groceries. It might be rolled oats warmed on the stove with a handful of walnuts and sliced fruit, or two slices of sturdy wholegrain toast topped with eggs and a side of greens. It could be plain unsweetened yogurt stirred with berries and pumpkin seeds, or even leftover lentils and rice from the night before. What matters is not novelty, but the combination of complex carbohydrates, steady protein, and satisfying fats that keep your blood sugar level and your mind clear.

When you eat a predictable, grounding meal before leaving the house, the rest of your day changes quietly. You arrive at lunchtime with steady hunger rather than frantic urgency, making it far easier to choose a balanced meal. The intense afternoon cravings that so often feel like personal weakness simply fail to materialize because your body was properly nourished hours earlier.

If your current mornings feel chaotic, resist the urge to overhaul your entire diet this week. Instead, pick one simple breakfast you know you can prepare on your busiest weekday morning, stock the necessary ingredients in your cupboard, and make it three days in a row. Sustainable nutrition is built through these small, unhurried domestic routines—one plain plate at a time.
